 Hochul announced applications are open for two student loan forgiveness programs 
 By Cali Johnson Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 3:21 PM EST | Updated : 18 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google NEW YORK (WBNG) — Gov. Kathy Hochul announced two New York State student loan forgiveness programs are now open. 
 The programs are designed to strengthen the state’s healthcare and agricultural workforces and help New Yorkers reduce their student loan debt.
 The Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program is open to applicants eligible for the 2025 program year and the Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program is open for the 2026 program year. 
 “From the nurses who train our future health care professionals to the farmers who help feed our families, New York depends on people who dedicate their careers to serving others,” Governor Hochul said. “Student debt shouldn’t stand in the way of their careers, and that’s what these loan forgiveness programs are all about. We’re investing in the people and industries that keep our communities strong, which is why I encourage eligible New Yorkers to apply and build their futures here in New York.”
 Strengthening New York’s Nursing Workforce
 The Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program aims to increase the number of qualified nursing faculty and adjunct clinical faculty teaching at nursing schools across the state. 
 With the program helping nursing educators repay their student loans, the program seeks to support the efforts of future nurses and strengthen the state’s health care workforce. 
 “Governor Hochul is strengthening health care in New York and the student loan forgiveness announced here today is the latest example of that commitment,” said New York State Health Commissioner Dr. James McDonald. “Removing student debt means more nurse educators will be able to train the next generation of our health care workforce and provide quality care to New Yorkers for years to come.”
 Eligible recipients may receive up to $8,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $40,000.
 To qualify, applicants must meet eligibility requirements, including:
 Be a registered nurse professionally licensed to practice in New York State. 
 Possess a master’s degree in nursing or a doctoral degree qualifying them to serve as nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty. 
 Have prior clinical experience as a licensed registered nurse. 
 Be employed as nursing faculty or adjunct clinical faculty at a nursing school in New York State, providing classroom or clinical instruction equivalent to at least 12 credit hours annually. 
 Have outstanding eligible student loan debt incurred while obtaining a nursing degree. 
 Meet other program eligibility requirements. 
 Supporting the Next Generation of New York Farmers
 The Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program helps college graduates pursue long-term careers in agriculture by reducing student loan debt. 
 The program aims to help New York’s agricultural workforce by encouraging graduates to start and maintain full-time farming operations in the state.
 New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets Commissioner Richard Ball said, “We have a terrific agricultural industry that is based in the strength of its innovative, hardworking farmers. The State, under the Governor’s leadership, has doubled down on its efforts to support the next generation of New York’s agricultural community, supporting our young people through agricultural education, investing in workforce development and ensuring critical resources are available to our beginning farmers. The Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program is another building block in these efforts, providing student loan forgiveness that can help new and young farmers clear the path to success in the industry.”
 Eligible recipients may receive up to $10,000 annually in student loan forgiveness for up to five years, with a maximum lifetime award of $50,000.
 To qualify, applicants must meet several requirements, including:
 Have earned an undergraduate degree from an approved New York State college or university. 
 Be within their first 10 years of operating a farm in New York State that produces agricultural products. 
 Operate a farm in New York State on a full-time basis and agree to continue doing so for at least five years. 
 Have outstanding eligible student loan debt associated with obtaining their undergraduate degree. 
 Meet other program eligibility requirements. 
 Applications for the Nursing Faculty Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program and Young Farmers Loan Forgiveness Incentive Program are open through Wednesday, Dec. 16, 2026. 
 Eligible New Yorkers must submit their applications before the deadline.
 For more information about eligibility requirements and to apply, visit HESC’s Loan Forgiveness Programs webpage.
